title: Moving Out, Moving Up: South Asian Migration to Amersham
episode_summary: James Staples and Luke Heslop travel from West London to Little Chalfont and Amersham to explore how South Asian migrants have moved out of traditional working-class areas such as Southall and Chesham into more affluent and rural parts of Buckinghamshire. They meet Vimal Dallal, who describes his family's migration from Gujarat to Southall in the 1980s, their early factory work, family-based support networks, property ownership, education, and eventual move to Little Chalfont. The episode also explores how the South Asian foodscape has changed in Amersham, with restaurants and shops increasingly reflecting the area's growing Indian, Hindu, and Jain communities. Through Vimal's story, the episode examines family sacrifice, social mobility, education, diaspora networks, nostalgia, and changing ideas of British Asian identity.
migration_themes: Migration from Gujarat to the UK
Migration from West London to Buckinghamshire
historical_topics: Growth of suburban South Asian communities
